resources.string: Applies to this playback. Switching briefly restarts video and keeps the position and pause state.
Applies to this channel. Switching briefly restarts playback at the live point.
Native HDR uses the direct Android video surface. GPU filters and Vulkan output are paused for this video.

HDR10 on an HDR10 display plays through Vulkan (gpu-next) with HDR passthrough, so HDR-safe shaders (sharpening, RAVU Lite / FSR) can run. Dolby Vision, HLG and HDR10+ on HDR10+ displays stay on the direct surface. If the HDR output cannot be confirmed or frames drop, the video reopens on the direct surface.
Process HDR on the GPU: HDR10 plays through Vulkan (gpu-next) with HDR passthrough.
Process HDR on the GPU: output “Direct” is selected.
Process HDR on the GPU: Dolby Vision stays on the direct surface.
Process HDR on the GPU: HDR10 only, this format stays on the direct surface.
Process HDR on the GPU: MPV Vulkan output is not available on this device.
Process HDR on the GPU: the Vulkan surface offers no HDR10.
Process HDR on the GPU: the display reports no HDR10, HDR is mapped to SDR.
Process HDR on the GPU: off in Low performance mode.
Process HDR on the GPU: HDR output was not confirmed, using the direct surface.
Process HDR on the GPU: too many dropped frames, using the direct surface.
HDR output through the GPU: sharpening, deband and the RAVU Lite / FSR upscalers apply. Film grain is off here; denoise, deblock, SSimSuperRes, picture adjustments and the other shaders need SDR.
Process HDR on the GPU: no HDR-safe shader or deband is selected, so HDR stays on the direct surface.
The default output “Direct” stays in place for SDR; HDR10 uses the GPU route as long as a shader or deband is selected. Choosing “Direct” in the player or a title profile keeps HDR direct.
HDR: only HDR-safe shaders (sharpening, RAVU Lite / FSR luma, deband) apply; chroma and SSim shaders are skipped.
